#!/bin/sh
# post-checkout hook
# Called after: git checkout, git switch, git clone
#
# Arguments:
#   $1 - Previous HEAD ref (before checkout)
#   $2 - New HEAD ref (after checkout)
#   $3 - Flag: 1 if branch checkout, 0 if file checkout

PREV_HEAD="$1"
NEW_HEAD="$2"
BRANCH_CHECKOUT="$3"

# Only run on branch checkouts (not file checkouts)
if [ "$BRANCH_CHECKOUT" = "1" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] Switched branch → $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"

  # Notify if package.json changed between refs
  if [ "$PREV_HEAD" != "$NEW_HEAD" ] && git diff --name-only "$PREV_HEAD" "$NEW_HEAD" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "package.json"; then
    echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  package.json changed — you may need to run: npm install"
  fi
fi

#!/bin/sh
# post-checkout hook
# Called after: git checkout, git switch, git clone
#
# Arguments:
#   $1 - Previous HEAD ref (before checkout)
#   $2 - New HEAD ref (after checkout)
#   $3 - Flag: 1 if branch checkout, 0 if file checkout

PREV_HEAD="$1"
NEW_HEAD="$2"
BRANCH_CHECKOUT="$3"

# Only run on branch checkouts (not file checkouts)
if [ "$BRANCH_CHECKOUT" = "1" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] Switched branch → $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"

  # Notify if package.json changed between refs
  if [ "$PREV_HEAD" != "$NEW_HEAD" ] && git diff --name-only "$PREV_HEAD" "$NEW_HEAD" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "package.json"; then
    echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  package.json changed — you may need to run: npm install"
  fi
fi

arguments.new_string:
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal service discovery endpoint probe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edit this list to match your internal services.
# Format: "label|url"
ENDPOINTS="
auth-service|http://localhost:4001/health
api-gateway|http://localhost:8080/health
user-service|http://localhost:4002/health
config-service|http://localhost:4003/health
discovery|http://localhost:8500/v1/status/leader
"

echo "[post-checkout] Probing internal service endpoints..."

ALL_OK=1
while IFS='|' read -r LABEL URL; do
  # Skip blank lines
  [ -z "$LABEL" ] && continue

  HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    --max-time 3 \
    --connect-timeout 2 \
    "$URL" 2>/dev/null)

  if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -ge 200 ] && [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -lt 300 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ✔ $LABEL ($URL) → $HTTP_STATUS"
  else
    echo "  ✘ $LABEL ($URL) → ${HTTP_STATUS:-unreachable}"
    ALL_OK=0
  fi
done <<EOF
$(echo "$ENDPOINTS" | grep -v '^\s*$')
EOF

if [ "$ALL_OK" = "0" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  One or more services are unreachable. Check your local stack."
else
  echo "[post-checkout] ✔ All services reachable."
fi

#!/bin/sh
# post-checkout hook
# Called after: git checkout, git switch, git clone
#
# Arguments:
#   $1 - Previous HEAD ref (before checkout)
#   $2 - New HEAD ref (after checkout)
#   $3 - Flag: 1 if branch checkout, 0 if file checkout

PREV_HEAD="$1"
NEW_HEAD="$2"
BRANCH_CHECKOUT="$3"

# Only run on branch checkouts (not file checkouts)
if [ "$BRANCH_CHECKOUT" = "1" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] Switched branch → $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"

  # Notify if package.json changed between refs

    echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  package.json changed — you may need to run: npm install"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal service discovery endpoint probe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edit this list to match your internal services.
# Format: "label|url"
ENDPOINTS="
auth-service|http://localhost:4001/health
api-gateway|http://localhost:8080/health
user-service|http://localhost:4002/health
config-service|http://localhost:4003/health
discovery|http://localhost:8500/v1/status/leader
"

echo "[post-checkout] Probing internal service endpoints..."

ALL_OK=1
while IFS='|' read -r LABEL URL; do
  # Skip blank lines
  [ -z "$LABEL" ] && continue

  HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    --max-time 3 \
    --connect-timeout 2 \
    "$URL" 2>/dev/null)

  if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -ge 200 ] && [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -lt 300 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ✔ $LABEL ($URL) → $HTTP_STATUS"
  else
    echo "  ✘ $LABEL ($URL) → ${HTTP_STATUS:-unreachable}"
    ALL_OK=0
  fi
done <<EOF
$(echo "$ENDPOINTS" | grep -v '^\s*$')
EOF

if [ "$ALL_OK" = "0" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  One or more services are unreachable. Check your local stack."
else
  echo "[post-checkout] ✔ All services reachable."
fi

Here's what the new block does:

**The `ENDPOINTS` list** — `label|url` pairs, one per line. Easy to extend — just add more rows. Currently probing five example services:
- `auth-service` → `:4001/health`
- `api-gateway` → `:8080/health`
- `user-service` → `:4002/health`
- `config-service` → `:4003/health`
- `discovery` (Consul-style) → `:8500/v1/status/leader`

**The loop:**
- Iterates each entry with `IFS='|'` splitting on the pipe delimiter
- `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"` — silent, discards body, captures HTTP status only
- `--max-time 3 / --connect-timeout 2` — won't hang the checkout if something's down
- 2xx → ✔ pass; anything else (including `000` for unreachable) → ✘ fail

**Summary line** at the end tells you at a glance if everything's healthy or not.

Just swap in your real endpoints in the `ENDPOINTS` block and you're good to go.

arguments.new_string:
STATUS_FILE="$HOME/.service-status"
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")

echo "[post-checkout] Probing internal service endpoints..."

# Write header to status file
{
  echo "# Service discovery status"
  echo "# Generated: $TIMESTAMP"
  echo "# Branch:    $BRANCH"
  echo "# Repo:      $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
  echo "#"
  printf "%-20s %-45s %-12s %s\n" "SERVICE" "URL" "STATUS" "RESULT"
  printf "%-20s %-45s %-12s %s\n" "-------" "---" "------" "------"
} > "$STATUS_FILE"

ALL_OK=1
while IFS='|' read -r LABEL URL; do
  # Skip blank lines
  [ -z "$LABEL" ] && continue

  HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    --max-time 3 \
    --connect-timeout 2 \
    "$URL" 2>/dev/null)

  if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -ge 200 ] && [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -lt 300 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    RESULT="OK"
    echo "  ✔ $LABEL ($URL) → $HTTP_STATUS"
  else
    RESULT="UNREACHABLE"
    HTTP_STATUS="${HTTP_STATUS:-000}"
    echo "  ✘ $LABEL ($URL) → $HTTP_STATUS"
    ALL_OK=0
  fi

  # Append row to status file
  printf "%-20s %-45s %-12s %s\n" "$LABEL" "$URL" "$HTTP_STATUS" "$RESULT" >> "$STATUS_FILE"

done <<EOF
$(echo "$ENDPOINTS" | grep -v '^\s*$')
EOF

# Write summary footer
{
  echo "#"
  if [ "$ALL_OK" = "0" ]; then
    echo "# SUMMARY: DEGRADED — one or more services unreachable"
  else
    echo "# SUMMARY: ALL OK"
  fi
} >> "$STATUS_FILE"

if [ "$ALL_OK" = "0" ]; then
  echo "[post-checkout] ⚠️  One or more services are unreachable. Check your local stack."
else
  echo "[post-checkout] ✔ All services reachable."
fi

echo "[post-checkout] Status saved → $STATUS_FILE"

content.text:
Done. Every time the hook runs, it writes a status snapshot to `~/.service-status`. Here's what the file looks like:

```
# Service discovery status
# Generated: 2026-05-20T13:54:00Z
# Branch:    main
# Repo:      /home/user/myproject
#
SERVICE              URL                                           STATUS       RESULT
-------              ---                                           ------       ------
auth-service         http://localhost:4001/health                  200          OK
api-gateway          http://localhost:8080/health                  000          UNREACHABLE
user-service         http://localhost:4002/health                  200          OK
config-service       http://localhost:4003/health                  200          OK
discovery            http://localhost:8500/v1/status/leader        200          OK
#
# SUMMARY: DEGRADED — one or more services unreachable
```

**Key details:**
- **File:** `~/.service-status` — hidden, in the home dir, overwritten fresh on each checkout
- **Header** includes timestamp (UTC ISO-8601), branch name, and repo path
- **Columns:** service label, URL, raw HTTP status code, and OK/UNREACHABLE result
- **Footer** gives a one-line SUMMARY — either `ALL OK` or `DEGRADED`
- The terminal output is unchanged — `$STATUS_FILE` path is echoed at the end so you always know where to look
